flags: Western Digital Corporation (WDC) completed the spin-off of Sandisk by distributing 116,035,464 shares, or 80.1%, of Sandisk's outstanding common stock to WDC stockholders while retaining 28,827,787 shares, or 19.9%, after which Sandisk began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol SNDK.

WDC disposed of its remaining Sandisk common stock through debt-for-equity exchanges of 21,314,768 shares (14.6%) and 5,821,135 shares, plus subsequent share exchanges, resulting in WDC having sold or exchanged all of its retained shares.

Sandisk entered into a Loan Agreement providing a $2.0 billion Term Loan B facility and a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility (including up to $150 million for letters of credit), borrowed $2.0 billion under the Term Loan Facility, and used part of the proceeds to make a $1.5 billion net distribution payment to WDC.
no_value_reason: no valuation route yet for a company with no operating profit in 3 of its last 4 fiscal years

business_model.claim: Sandisk is a vertically integrated global semiconductor memory company with more than 30 years of innovation in NAND flash technology, owning chip-level design, IP, front and back-end manufacturing, and systems engineering.
quotes: Sandisk is a leading global semiconductor memory company with more than 30 years of innovation in NAND flash technology.
We are a vertically integrated solutions provider with ownership of chip-level design and IP, front and back-end manufacturing, as well as systems engineering and design.

business_model.claim: Following its separation from Western Digital Corporation, Sandisk sells products primarily under the Sandisk brand and, for a limited transitional period, under licensed Western Digital and WD brands.
quotes: Our broad portfolio of technology and products addresses multiple end markets of “Datacenter,” “Edge” and “Consumer” and are comprised of the Sandisk™ brand.
Certain of our products will also be sold for a limited transitional period under the Western Digital®, WD® and other brands under license from WDC.

business_model.claim: Sandisk's product portfolio consists of solid-state drives (SSDs), embedded products, removable cards, universal serial bus drives, and wafers and components.
quotes: Our solutions include a broad range of solid-state drives (“SSDs”), embedded products, removable cards, universal serial bus drives and wafers and components.

business_model.claim: In the Datacenter end market, Sandisk sells high-performance enterprise-class SSDs and software solutions to public or private cloud environments, cloud service providers, and enterprise customers for servers, online transactions, AI workloads, and data analysis.
quotes: The Datacenter end market is comprised primarily of products for public or private cloud environments and enterprise customers.

Our high-performance enterprise class SSDs include high-performance flash-based SSDs and software solutions that are optimized for performance applications providing a range of capacity and performance levels primarily for use in enterprise servers and supporting high-volume online transactions, AI-related workloads, data analysis and other enterprise applications.

business_model.claim: In the Edge end market, Sandisk sells SSDs and flash-based embedded storage products to OEM and channel customers for personal computers, mobile devices, gaming consoles, automotive, physical AI, connected home, and industrial applications.
quotes: Through the Edge end market, we provide our original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”) and channel customers a broad array of high-performance flash solutions across personal computer, mobile, gaming, automotive, physical AI, at-home entertainment, and industrial spaces.

Through the Edge end market, we provide numerous data solutions that we incorporate into our client’s devices, which consist of SSDs for desktop and notebook PCs, gaming consoles and set top boxes, as well as flash-based embedded storage products for mobile phones, tablets, notebook PCs and other portable and wearable devices, automotive applications, Internet of Things, and industrial and connected home applications.

business_model.claim: In the Consumer end market, Sandisk sells portable SSDs, removable cards, and universal serial bus flash drives to end users through retail and channel routes.
quotes: We serve the Consumer end market with a portfolio of SSDs and removable flash products, including cards and universal serial bus flash drives, through our retail and channel routes to market.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3 and P4.
business_model.claim: AI infrastructure expansion and AI adoption are primary demand drivers, lifting storage demand, pricing, and strategic product allocation across end markets.
quotes: In the first quarter, we continued to observe that the rapid growth of AI infrastructure is driving demand for high-performance storage products, and AI adoption is driving the need for NAND storage to support these workloads, leading to increased revenues when compared to prior periods.
The current environment and market demand have led to pricing and product mix shifts, including strategic decisions about how we allocate products to customers across the end markets we serve.

business_model.claim: In 2026, net revenue rose 175%, or $12,893 million, compared to 2025, driven by a 437% increase in Datacenter revenue, a 195% increase in Edge revenue, and a 29% increase in Consumer revenue as higher pricing offset lower Consumer unit sales.
quotes: Net revenue increased 175%, or $12,893 million, in 2026 compared to 2025, due to a 437% increase in Datacenter revenue, a 195% increase in Edge revenue, and a 29% increase in Consumer revenue.
Consumer revenue increased 29%, or $667 million in 2026 compared to 2025, primarily due to higher pricing partially offset by lower sales.

business_model.claim: Sandisk records sales incentives, price protection, and marketing reimbursements as reductions of gross revenue, which represented 11% of gross revenues in 2026 compared to 19% in 2025 and 2024.
quotes: Consistent with standard industry practice, we offer sales incentives and marketing programs that provide customers with price protection and other incentives or reimbursements that are recorded as reductions of gross revenue.
For 2026, 2025 and 2024, these programs represented 11%, 19%, and 19%, respectively, of gross revenues.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3, P4, and P10.
business_model.claim: Starting in the second half of fiscal year 2026, Sandisk entered into multi-year New Business Model (NBM) agreements with Datacenter and Edge customers that commit stated volumes with fixed and variable pricing mechanisms and financial guarantees.
quotes: Commencing in the second half of fiscal year 2026, we entered into long-term agreements, which we also refer to as New Business Models, or “NBMs,” with several Datacenter and Edge customers.
These agreements generally commit us to deliver, and our customers to purchase, a stated volume of products, mostly over multi-year periods.

The agreements include pricing mechanisms consisting of fixed and variable components and are supported by financial guarantees that are intended to provide additional protection in the event a customer does not satisfy their contractual purchase obligations.

business_model.claim: Competitive industry conditions—including declining average selling prices, volatile demand, industry cycles, and customer deployment timing—can cause Sandisk's revenue and operating results to fluctuate.
quotes: Competitive conditions, including declining average selling prices, volatile demand, technological change, industry consolidation, lengthy product qualifications, and supply constraints, in our industry can negatively impact our business.

Our operating results may fluctuate due to changes in demand, industry cycles and the timing of customer deployments, including AI-related data center investments, and our ability to accurately forecast demand as a result of these changing market conditions.

business_model.claim: Sandisk obtains all of its flash-based memory wafers from its 49.9%-owned Flash Ventures joint ventures with Kioxia in Japan at cost plus a small markup, paying variable costs on rolling forecasts and half of Flash Ventures' fixed costs regardless of output purchased.
quotes: All of our flash-based memory is obtained from our joint ventures with Kioxia, which provide us with leading-edge, high-quality flash memory wafers.
We hold a 49.9% ownership position in each of the Flash Ventures entities.
The price that we and Kioxia pay Flash Ventures for flash memory wafers is cost plus a small markup.
We are obligated to pay for variable costs incurred in producing our share of Flash Ventures’ flash-based memory wafer supply based on a rolling forecast.
In addition, we are obligated to pay for half of Flash Ventures’ fixed costs regardless of the output we choose to purchase.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P1 and P2.
business_model.claim: Sandisk designs controllers primarily in-house using third-party foundries or suppliers, conducts assembly and test at its Penang, Malaysia facility, contract manufacturers, and 20%-owned SDSS, and relies on external suppliers for components such as DRAM.
quotes: Controllers are primarily designed in-house and manufactured by third-party foundries or acquired from third-party suppliers.

Our assembly and test operations comprise in-house assembly and test facilities located in Penang, Malaysia, facilities operated by other contract manufacturers, and the assembly and test facility owned and operated by SDSS, a venture that is owned 20% by Sandisk and 80% by JCET Management Co., Ltd.
For example, many of our enterprise-grade SSD products incorporate DRAM, which is a commodity component that has experienced supply constraints and may remain in short supply for extended periods.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3 and P6, with cost of revenue figures verified in F2, P3, and P4.
business_model.claim: Higher sales and pricing drove substantial gross margin expansion: in 2026, gross profit margin increased 4,100 basis points over 2025 as cost of revenue moved from 5,143 (table in millions) to 5,776 (table in millions), and in Q1 2027 GAAP gross margin reached 85.0% compared to 29.8% a year earlier.
quotes: Gross profit margin increased 4,100 basis points in 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to higher sales and higher pricing.

business_model.claim: In 2026, research and development expenses increased $196 million and selling, general and administrative expenses increased $103 million over 2025, driven primarily by performance-based variable compensation and headcount, partially offset in SG&A by a $51 million materials decrease from selling qualification units rather than distributing free samples.
quotes: Research and development (“R&D”) expenses increased $196 million in 2026 compared to 2025, primarily due to a $136 million increase in compensation and benefits due to variable compensation associated with company performance and increased headcount, a $28 million increase in spending for R&D projects as we continue to invest in innovation, and a $24 million increase in stock based compensation.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $103 million in 2026 compared to 2025, primarily due to a $68 million increase in compensation and benefits due to variable compensation associated with company performance and increased headcount, partially offset by a $51 million decrease in materials due to a change in business practice for the launch of new products whereby the Company is distributing fewer free samples and has started entering into contracts to sell certain qualification units to customers.
The costs of qualification units are recorded in inventory until sold to customers and recognized as cost of revenue.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P2 and P4.
business_model.claim: Sandisk's cost of goods sold and operating margins are exposed to potential tariff increases or loss of U.S. tariff exemptions under Section 232 and Section 301 investigations, facility disruptions causing under-absorbed overhead, and currency exchange rate fluctuations.
quotes: Currently, the majority of our products sold in the U.S. are exempt from tariffs, but additional tariff increases, or the loss of applicable exemptions, would increase the cost of goods sold for our products sold in the U.S., which could negatively impact our margins and financial performance.

Impacts of any of these events may also include closures of our manufacturing facilities, under-absorbed overhead, increased logistics, component and other costs, decreased demand for our products, and manufacturing challenges, delays in production ramps, and interruptions or inefficiencies in our operations.
Fluctuations in currency exchange rates may negatively affect our operating results.

quotes: Commencing in the second half of fiscal year 2026, we entered into long-term agreements, which we also refer to as New Business Models, or “NBMs,” with several Datacenter and Edge customers.
These agreements generally commit us to deliver, and our customers to purchase, a stated volume of products, mostly over multi-year periods.

quotes: We compete with vertically-integrated suppliers such as Kioxia, Micron Technology, Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., SK Hynix, Inc., Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. and numerous smaller companies that assemble flash into products.

Competitive conditions, including declining average selling prices, volatile demand, technological change, industry consolidation, lengthy product qualifications, and supply constraints, in our industry can negatively impact our business.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Dependence on a limited number of qualified and sometimes sole-source suppliers—including extended DRAM supply constraints for enterprise SSDs—threatens product mix, revenues, and gross margins.
quotes: Many of the components and much of the equipment we acquire must be specifically designed for use in our products or for developing and manufacturing our products and are only available from a limited number of suppliers, some of whom are our sole-source suppliers.
For example, many of our enterprise-grade SSD products incorporate DRAM, which is a commodity component that has experienced supply constraints and may remain in short supply for extended periods.
Such constraints could adversely affect our product mix, revenues, gross margins, customer relationships and competitive position.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: High-volume manufacturing operations in Japan, Malaysia, and elsewhere in Asia are exposed to natural disasters, geopolitical disruptions, and potential underinsurance.
quotes: We conduct our operations at large, high-volume, purpose-built facilities in Japan, Malaysia and other locations in Asia.

We maintain limited insurance coverage and, in some cases, no coverage at all, for natural disasters and damage to our facilities, as these types of insurance are sometimes not available or available only at a prohibitive cost.
We depend upon Kioxia to obtain and maintain sufficient property, business interruption and other insurance for Flash Ventures.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q1 2027 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Pending U.S. trade investigations under Section 232 and Section 301 could remove tariff exemptions on U.S. sales, increasing cost of goods sold and potentially reducing demand.
quotes: There are pending and ongoing investigations initiated by the United States under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 that may impact tariff rates for our products.

Though the majority of our products sold in the U.S. are currently exempt from tariffs, additional tariff increases or the loss of applicable exemptions would increase the cost of goods sold for our products sold in the U.S., which could negatively impact our margins and financial performance.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Retention of senior leaders and specialized NAND engineering talent is threatened by global competition for AI-era expertise and potential leadership attrition when materially appreciated equity awards vest in February 2028 or September 2028.
quotes: The rapid pace of innovation driven by AI, global research and development competition, evolving models of work, and intensifying customer demands for faster, more efficient solutions has significantly raised the bar for the technical expertise required to power current and next-generation technologies.
These awards generally vest either in February 2028 or September 2028.
If the value of these awards at such time remains materially appreciated above their grant date values, we could experience attrition among these leaders when the awards vest.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.

quotes: If an epidemic failure occurs, we may face termination of long-term sales agreements and may be required to replace or refund the value of the defective product and to cover certain other costs associated with the consequences of the epidemic failure.

In addition, product defects, product recalls or epidemic failures may cause damage to our reputation or customer relationships, lost revenue, indemnification for a recall of our customers’ products, warranty claims, litigation or loss of market share with our customers, including our OEMs and OEM customers.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.

Our increasing use of AI, including generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled automation technologies, may elevate the risk of cybersecurity incidents, whether through our authorized use of such technologies to perform business or operational tasks with limited human oversight or through malicious use by threat actors to automate, scale or adapt attacks against our systems, products, employees, customers, suppliers or partners.
